what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: The homepage rebuild now leads with real vaults
sections.para: The previous article found a homepage that led with encryption and buried twenty-five real vaults under a table. This is the promised rebuild, set beside those screenshots: what moved, what was cut, what it is generated from, and the one thing it still cannot show.

sections.label: The first screen
sections.line: The first screen now shows four real vaults
sections.para: The old opening was an encryption claim, a pip install and a familiar four-command terminal walkthrough. Now one sentence frames a vault as a unit of work: data, app, history and sources, shipped as one string. Encryption became a subordinate clause, and a hero field in the vault data picks the four cards.

sections.label: The use cases became things
sections.line: Use cases became six real vaults, none about encryption
sections.para: Five category cards were replaced by six vaults chosen by the job they do. None of the six lines mentions encryption: a pentest report with its retest scripts, a talk that keeps its cited papers, a game using a publishable credential. These are properties of a vault as a unit, which a newcomer can feel.

sections.label: The collaboration story got a front door
sections.line: The collaboration band's numbers come from site data
sections.para: A log once filed under Docs became a homepage band with numbers and a story. None of the numbers is typed: releases come from the version log, vaults from the vault data, sites from the network directory, briefs from counting the briefs page. A wrong number means the site is wrong elsewhere too.

sections.label: What was cut
sections.line: Three bands cut, three added, nine bands remain
sections.para: The abstract use-case band and the "One vault, three doors" band were cut to a nav entry and a pill. The terminal walkthrough moved down under "Under the hood, it is git" and gained an apps-live-inside-the-data card. Nine bands before and after, corrected in v0.2.61; words fell from 1,370 to 1,332.

sections.label: What it cannot show yet
sections.line: No published vault yet shows agents sharing one history
sections.para: The rebuild did not close the gap the previous article named: no published vault shows two agents on one vault, with their branches and a human merging them. The team band shows agents building for each other, not with each other, and is written not to pretend otherwise. That vault will go in the hero.

sections.label: What it is generated from
sections.line: One data file now drives the whole homepage
sections.para: admin/content/vaults.json drives the hero cards, the six jobs, the sortable table and the vault count. Adding a vault is adding a row, and promoting one is setting a field. The homepage became a view over the site's own data, the rule the articles band, network directory and update feed already followed.
